claude.sample_unit: simulated patient scenarios (MEWS triage); 264 scenarios for department guidance

links.outcome: Run-to-run consistency (Kendall correlation) of MEWS scoring across 10 repeated runs, before vs after prompt engineering
links.effect: GPT-4-Turbo mean Kendall coefficient improved from 0.6176 (SD 0.2135) to 1.00 (SD 0); GPT-4o improved from 0.8327 to 0.8646 (not significant, P=.32).
links.quote: For GPT-4-Turbo, the mean value dramatically improved from 0.6176 (SD 0.2135) in trial 1 to 1.00 (SD 0) in trial 2.

links.outcome: MEWS scoring accuracy of GPT-4 models compared with nurses' manual calculation
links.effect: GPT-4o accuracy after prompt engineering was 96.20% vs 81.8% for nurses' manual calculation from a previous study; GPT-4-Turbo reached 100%.
links.quote: This is particularly notable when compared to the finding of a previous study, which indicated that the overall accuracy rate of nurses’ manual calculations was 81.8% [ 20 ].

links.outcome: Arithmetic errors in summing MEWS parameter scores by unoptimized prompts
links.effect: Before prompt engineering, overall accuracy was 63.41% (GPT-4o) and 63.93% (GPT-4-Turbo); the model often failed to sum correct parameter scores.
links.quote: Despite accurately determining individual parameter scores, ChatGPT frequently failed to sum them accurately.

links.outcome: Accuracy of triage scoring and department guidance in simulated emergency department scenarios
links.effect: Triage accuracy 96.2%-100% after prompt engineering; department guidance accuracy 92.63% (95% CI 90.34%-94.93%), lowest in dermatology (79.57%); miscalculations of 1-2 points could miss patients needing immediate care.
links.quote: Minor deviation of 1 or 2 scores in the MEWS can lead to overlooking patients needing immediate care or providing unnecessary treatment, thus wasting medical resources [ 29 ].

links.outcome: Adherence to prompt constraints (single department, predefined list) in department guidance
links.effect: Despite repeating instructions in every query, the model sometimes recommended multiple departments or departments outside the predefined list.
links.quote: Despite these measures, instances of the model recommending multiple departments still occurred.

links.outcome: MEWS scoring accuracy after clarifying input data usage and format via prompt engineering
links.effect: Accuracy rose from 63.93% to 100% (GPT-4-Turbo) and 63.41% to 96.20% (GPT-4o) after prompt revision addressing confused parameters and AVPU conversion.
links.quote: The results from both GPT-4o and GPT-4-Turbo models in trial 2 showed significant improvement ( Figure 2 ).

links.outcome: MEWS triage accuracy before vs after prompt engineering with structured prompt
links.effect: GPT-4-Turbo accuracy rose from 63.93% to 100%; GPT-4o from 63.41% to 96.20%; average difference from standard score fell to 0 and 0.08.
links.quote: GPT-4-Turbo achieved an impressive accuracy of 100% across all the 10 runs.

links.outcome: Overreliance on patient medical history in department guidance errors
links.effect: Physicians attributed 43.42% of overall guidance errors to overreliance on patient medical history rather than current symptoms.
links.quote: Another key finding in this part of the experiment was that the guidance provided by ChatGPT (GPT-4o model) was sometimes influenced by the medical history of patients, where physicians attributed 43.42% of the overall guidance error to an overreliance on the medical history of patients.

unlisted_practices: Including restrictive instruction prompt in every query to prevent instruction forgetting
Using Python tool for arithmetic calculations to avoid summation errors

links.outcome: MEWS scoring accuracy after prompt engineering
links.effect: Accuracy improved from 63.93% to 100% for GPT-4-Turbo and 63.41% to 96.20% for GPT-4o.
links.quote: ChatGPT's triage accuracy, based on MEWS, improved following prompt engineering.

links.effect: GPT-4o Kendall mean 0.8327 to 0.8646; GPT-4-Turbo 0.6176 to 1.00 after prompt engineering.
links.quote: For GPT-4-Turbo, the mean value dramatically improved from 0.6176 (SD 0.2135) in trial 1 to 1.00 (SD 0) in trial 2.

links.effect: Post-prompt GPT-4-Turbo triage 100%; GPT-4o triage 96.20%; GPT-4o department guidance 92.63%.
links.quote: The overall accuracy for the 3 major departments was 92.63% (95% CI 90.34%-94.93%), with internal medicine departments achieving the highest accuracy of 93.51% (95% CI 90.85%-96.17%).

links.effect: After prompt engineering, GPT-4-Turbo achieved 100% triage accuracy versus GPT-4o 96.2%.
links.quote: GPT-4-Turbo achieved an accuracy of 100% compared to GPT-4o's accuracy of 96.2%, despite GPT-4o initially showing better performance prior to prompt engineering.

unlisted_practices: Including the restrictive clinical prompt in every query to reduce forgetting of prior instructions
Using an LLM’s Python plugin or explicit computation instructions for MEWS score summation

links.outcome: triage scoring accuracy variation across repeated runs
links.effect: accuracy across 10 runs ranged 27.18%-76.05% (overall 63.41%) for GPT-4o and 26.59%-96.60% (overall 63.93%) for GPT-4-Turbo
links.quote: For GPT-4o, grading accuracy ranged from 27.18% (run 9) to 76.05% (runs 2 and 10), with an overall accuracy of 63.41%.

screen.practice: prompt engineering to improve triage accuracy
screen.reason: Evaluated the performance of LLMs (GPT-4o, GPT-4-Turbo) for emergency department triage and outpatient guidance on simulated clinical scenarios, explicitly testing outcomes before and after prompt engineering.
